CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  April 6, 2020 - 2:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 30, 2020 at 2:00 p.m., and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Tomek called the special meeting to order at 2:07 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by City Attorney/City Prosecutor
  Michele Beal Bagneris.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Terry Tomek
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Victor Gordo
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Margaret McAustin
  Councilmember Andy Wilson

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

RECOMMENDATIONS  ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ALTERNATE CARE FACILITY TO
FROM OFFICERS AND  TREAT COVID-19 PATIENTS
DEPARTMENTS  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the recommended action is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") pursuant to State
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15269 (emergency projects), and
  Section 15301 (existing facilities); and,
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract with
  Redrock Entertainment Services, in an amount not-to-exceed
  $700,000 without competitive bidding pursuant to City Charter
  Section 1002(G), contracts for labor, material, or supplies for actual
  emergency work, and Pasadena Municipal Code Section 4.08.049,
  subdivisions (A)(6), labor, material, supplies or services for actual
  emergency work and (B), contracts for which the City's best
  interests are served, to furnish and deliver equipment necessary to
  establish a Temporary Medical Facility at the Pasadena Center for
  a three month period; (Contract No. 37100)
  (3) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a zero-dollar
  Services Agreement with Pasadena Hospital Association (dba
  Huntington Memorial Hospital) without competitive selection
  pursuant to Pasadena Municipal Code Section 4.08.049,
  subdivisions (A)(6), labor, material, supplies or services for actual
  emergency work and (B), contracts for which the City's best
  interests are served, for the operation of the Temporary Medical

Council Minutes  1  04/06/2020
   Facility, during the pendency of its establishment at the Pasadena
  Center; and, (Contract No. 23,340)
  (4) Appropriate $700,000 from the City's 5% General Fund
  reserve to the non-departmental portion of the Fiscal Year 2020
  Operating Budget.(Budget Amendment No. 2020-36)

  City Manager Mermell summarized the agenda report as part of his
  oral presentation, and responded to questions. Lori J. Morgan,
  M.D., President and CEO of Huntington Memorial Hospital,
  provided  information  on  state-mandated  hospital  bed
  requirements, and details regarding the establishment of a
  Temporary Medical Facility at the Pasadena Conference Center in
  partnership with the City; and responded to questions. Javan Rad,
  Chief Assistant City Attorney, responded to questions related to the
  liabilities and risks. Bryan Frieders, Acting Fire Chief, responded
  to questions related to floor layout at the Temporary Medical
  Facility, and the selection process for the contractor to setup the
  Facility. Dr. Ying-Ying Goh, Director of Public Health, provided
  information on COVID-19 local and regional illness projections, and
  responded to questions.

  In response to Councilmember Kennedy's inquiry related to the
  status of the Pasadena Center Operating Company (PCOC)
  insurance policy, City Attorney Bagneris stated that PCOC has a
  special liability insurance policy coverage up to $3 million with the
  City, and stated that she will confirm whether the Temporary
  Medical Facility will fall within the scope of the current policy.

  Councilmember Wilson asked staff to be mindful of the concerns
  of adjacent residents to the Conference Center, and ensure that
  the security plan addresses patient transportation to and from
  PCOC to maximize public safety and mitigate risks.

  Councilmember Gordo asked HMH staff to provide information on
  the number of COVID-19 patients that have recovered and have
  been discharged from the hospital.

  Councilmember Madison asked staff to provide him with copies of
  the contract with Redrock Entertainment Services.

  Vice Mayor Hampton asked staff to ensure that HMH only utilize
  the Temporary Medical Facility as a worst case scenario basis.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that two letters were received in favor
  of the staff recommendation, with one letter in opposition, and with
  all letters distributed to the City Council, posted online, and made
  part of the record for this item. In addition, a public comment from
  Vincent DeRosa, Pasadena resident, was read aloud expressing
  public safety concerns for adjacent residents related to the
  proposed Temporary Medical Facility.

Council Minutes  2  04/06/2020
   Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember McAustin,
  seconded by Councilmember Kennedy, to approve the staff
  recommendation:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton, Mayor
  Tomek
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  City Manager Mermell reported that at the next City Council
  meeting, staff will provide an update on the City's proposed meal
  program and reported that staff is working with small restaurants
  and connecting them with business opportunities to provide meals,
  and is working with nine food providers in the City to develop meal
  programs.

CONSENT ITEM  AUTHORIZATION  TO  ENTER  INTO  A  STANDARD
DISCUSSED SEPARATELY  AGREEMENT WITH THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA TO RECEIVE
  $105,625.89 IN COVID-19 EMERGENCY RESPONSE GRANT
  FUNDS
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the recommended action is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") pursuant to State
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), the "General Rule" that
  CEQA only applies to projects that may have an effect on the
  environment;
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract with the
  State of California Business, Consumer Services, and Housing
  Agency (BCSH) for the receipt of emergency funding in the amount
  of $105,625.89 to protect the health and safety of people
  experiencing homelessness and reduce the spread of the COVID-
  19 outbreak; and (Contract No. 23,338)
  (3) Amend the Fiscal Year (FY) 2020 Operating Budget to
  recognize revenues and appropriate expenditures in the amount of
  $105,625.89. (Budget Amendment No. 2020-35)

  William Huang, Housing Director, reported that the proposed
  funding is designated specifically to slow the spread of COVID-19
  by providing emergency housing to highly vulnerable individuals
  who are homeless; provided information on actions to house such

Council Minutes  4  04/06/2020
   individuals, plans to setup mobile showers and handwashing
  stations; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Wilson requested that staff provide additional
  information regarding the proposed action, including allocation of
  funds, available resources to support housing the homeless, and
  strategies and regulations for addressing any issues that may arise
  once individuals are housed.

  Vice Mayor Hampton suggested that temporary housing units be
  centrally located so that service providers can provide assistance
  to as many homeless individuals as possible.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Wilson
  seconded by Councilmember Masuda, to approve the staff
  recommendation:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton, Mayor
  Tomek
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

RECOMMENDATIONS FROM ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION SUSPENDING COLLECTION
OFFICERS AND  OF THE LIGHT AND POWER SURTAX ("UNDERGROUND
DEPARTMENTS  SURTAX") FOR A PERIOD EQUAL TO SIX MONTHLY OR
  THREE BI-MONTHLY UTILITY BILLING CYCLES EFFECTIVE
Continued  UPON ADOPTION OF THE RESOLUTION AND PROVIDING
  FOR CUSTOMER REBATES
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is not a project subject to
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) as defined in Section

Council Minutes  5  04/06/2020
   21065 of CEQA and Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines
  and, as such, no environmental document pursuant to CEQA is
  required for the project; and
  (2) Adopt a resolution suspending the collection of the Light and
  Power Surtax ("Underground Surtax") for a period equal to six
  monthly or three bi-monthly utility billing cycles effective upon
  adoption of the Resolution and providing for customer rebates.
  (Resolution No. 9776)

  City Manager Mermell summarized the staff report as part of his
  oral presentation; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember McAustin spoke in favor  of  the  staff
  recommendation to help local businesses.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that five letters were received in favor
  of the staff recommendation, with two letters providing comments
  and concerns, and with all letters distributed to the City Council,
  posted online, and made part of the record for this item. In addition,
  a public comment from Paul Little, President of the Pasadena
  Chamber of Commerce, was read aloud in support of the staff
  recommendation, and advocated for additional financial support for
  local small businesses in Pasadena.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Wilson
  seconded by Councilmember Masuda, to approve the staff
  recommendation:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton, Mayor
  Tomek
  NOES:  None

  ABSTAIN: None

INFORMATION ITEM  PREDEVELOPMENT PLAN REVIEW OF A SINGLE-ROOM
  OCCUPANCY BUILDING PROPOSED AT 274-282 NORTH
  OAKLAND AVENUE
  Recommendation: This report is intended to provide information
  to the City Council; no action is required.

  Mayor Tomek summarized correspondence from Pasadena
  Studios LLC and Bridge Financial Advisors, noting that the
  proposed project no longer requires conditional use permits, or
  variance and is intending to use the City's incentives.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that one letter was received providing
  comments and expressing concerns related to the proposed
  project, which was distributed to the City Council, posted online
  and made part of the record for this item.

  Councilmember Kennedy requested that the item return to the City
  Council, asking that the project developers also participate and
  have an opportunity to respond to questions regarding the
  proposed project.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
